An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 9 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 10 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 11 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 12 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 13 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 14 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 15 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 16 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 17 18 API 19 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 20 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 23 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 24 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 25 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 26 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 27 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 28 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 29 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 30 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 31 32 Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 33 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 34 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 35 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 36 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 37 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 38 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 39 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 40 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 41 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 42 10. pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

content.text:
The server matches the spec on every point I checked, and I found no spec violation. The only real issues are structural: `server.mjs` has no export boundary, and the test file is large. I didn't re-run the suite (it passed 142/142 per your note). I did run coverage on `test/server.test.mjs` alone.

**Spec conformance.** I read these against the code and found them correct:
- **Startup:** the order is PORT, then data file, then listen. The `cannot read data file <name>` message uses the name as given. ENOENT yields an empty store, and the stdout line is the only stdout write.
- **Status codes and messages:** the 415, 413, 400 and 409 replies and their messages are exact.
- **Rule order and counting:** rule order is respected, and 413 counts bytes received.
- **Body draining:** the body is drained before every reply, including 404 and 405.
- **Save and serialization:** writes are serialized through a queue. A failed write returns 500 without advancing the id or the in-memory store.

**Where it falls short:**
- **Coverage figure:** the 51% server.mjs line coverage in the report is a measurement artifact, not a real gap. The tests spawn `server.mjs` as a subprocess, so `--experimental-test-coverage` can't see it. Behavioural coverage is thorough: the test titles cover every rule, plus persistence, rollback, concurrency and startup order.
- **Structure and size:** `server.mjs` is 315 lines with validation, store, HTTP and startup in one file. Nothing is exported, so none of it can be unit-tested directly. `test/server.test.mjs` is 715 lines, over the 400 typical but under the 800 max.
- **Errors:** `commit` (server.mjs:189) and the `loadStore` caller (server.mjs:304) discard the original error. Both are user-facing by spec, but nothing is logged. A listen `error` event after startup (server.mjs:309) only sets `exitCode`, so the server keeps running.
- **Minor:** `writeFile` truncates the file in place (server.mjs:188), so a crash mid-write can corrupt it. The `/^[1-9][0-9]*$/` check at server.mjs:209 is redundant with the `String(b.id)` comparison.

## GRADE
Overall: 8/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 8 — clear helpers, immutable stores, route under 50 lines; one file mixes validation, store, HTTP and startup
naming: 9 — descriptive and consistent
duplication: 9 — validators shared between requests and data-file loading
size: 7 — server.mjs 315 lines is fine; server.test.mjs at 715 lines is over the 400 typical
errors: 8 — exact spec messages and codes, ENOENT told apart; the original error is dropped in commit and in the load catch, and a post-start listen error does not exit
tests: 8 — thorough behavioural tests with wrong-implementation traps, but the subprocess design means server.mjs coverage can't be measured
security: 9 — no injection surface, body size capped, own-property checks guard `__proto__`, path fixed
leftovers: 10 — no console, TODO or dead code
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-daaee26c/server.mjs:309 on a listen error after startup, exit rather than only setting exitCode (call `process.exit(1)` or close the server)
- /root/bench-runs/h4-daaee26c/server.mjs:188 write to a temp file and rename it, so a crash mid-save can't corrupt the data file
- /root/bench-runs/h4-daaee26c/server.mjs:209 drop the redundant regex or document why it is there
- /root/bench-runs/h4-daaee26c/test/server.test.mjs:1 split into startup, API and booking-rules files to get under about 400 lines each
- /root/bench-runs/h4-daaee26c/server.mjs:1 consider moving validation and store code into a module that can be unit-tested in-process and covered
